# HEN Morning Analysis — 2026-08-27
**Hunt Energy Network | ERCOT BESS Fleet (32 Nodes)**
*Prepared: Pre-Market | Ref Date: 2026-08-27 | Settlement Ref: 2026-08-26*

---

## 1. PERFORMANCE SUMMARY

Yesterday marked a decisive regime shift for the HEN fleet. After two consecutive low-price days (RT avg $36.14 on 8/24; $31.83 on 8/25 with only 1 spike node), the fleet snapped back hard on 8/26 — fleet average RT surged to **$125.48/MWh**, all 32 nodes registered above $100/MWh spike conditions, and the fleet peak hit **$809.10/MWh**. This is the most broadly elevated RT pricing day in the recent 3-day window, suggesting a return of afternoon heat-driven scarcity consistent with 90.2 GW gross load and constrained transmission in South/West Texas.

**DART interpretation is critical today.** Every node in the fleet posted a **negative DART** (RT exceeded DA across the board), meaning the DA market systematically underpriced yesterday's RT scarcity. The "Top 5 DART Performers" labeled in the data are actually the nodes where RT *least* exceeded DA — CATARINA_B1 (RT exceeded DA by $29.99/MWh) and TYNAN_RN (RT exceeded DA by $36.86/MWh) were the smallest RT outperformers. Conversely, the "Bottom 5" — JUNCTION_RN (RT exceeded DA by **$106.99/MWh**), RUSSEKST_RN ($82.57), TOYAH_RN ($81.67), GOMZ_RN ($81.14), and SANDLAKE_RN ($81.03) — were the **strongest RT outperformers** on the fleet, capturing materially higher real-time prices than their DA commitments. Any assets dispatched in RT at these nodes captured significant premium. CATARINA_B1 and TYNAN_RN both recorded negative price episodes, tempering their RT revenue despite the broader scarcity event.

---

The 7-day forecast is unambiguously bullish for ERCOT prices and HEN RT dispatch. Temperatures across all major load centers remain 98–107°F through September 2, with **no meaningful cooling relief in sight**. Laredo leads at 107°F today, Abilene at 101–103°F through the week, and DFW holding 98–102°F daily — all well above normal late-August climatology. This thermal regime supports gross loads sustaining at or above 90 GW through the weekend and into next week.

The **Lubbock/Midland region** (relevant to West Texas BESS nodes including TOYAH_RN, SANDLAKE_RN, CEDRVALE_RN) carries elevated precip probability today (47–59%) — afternoon convective activity could temporarily suppress solar output and drive RT spikes, but may also reduce afternoon temperatures and load. Wind generation at 21.1 GW remains healthy, partially offsetting heat-driven demand pressure, but solar at 29.6 GW will ramp down by HE18–HE19, creating the classic Texas "evening cliff" that has driven the HE20–HE22 constraint binding patterns observed yesterday.

**Coastal and South Texas** (relevant to CATARINA_B1, TYNAN_RN, POTEETS_RN, FALFUR_RN) shows elevated precip probability through the week (Brownsville 13–36%, Corpus Christi 12–21%), which could introduce load uncertainty and transmission variability on the South Texas pathways.
